black cotton thread used by women for plaiting the hair
cotton wool, plant, thread; cf. Sugia 9 for Songhai origin
sickness characterized by constant severe headache; sufferer often shaves his hair to apply medicine (= okịlị ịgba isi)
an Igbo market day, following Èke, personified as an alụ̄ṣị
friend; lover; mistress; adultery (more common than enyi and ọwi)
ivory bracelet worn by titled man
filter (of fibre-sponge, ògbo); tow-like filter (cf. nzà, gauze filter) (from -zà 2. filter)
title entitling holder to be called nzè; title of high degree, and much coveted, conferring on the owner privileges and honour as a sacrosanct being
to force way through small doorway, small opening in wall, thicket
enter into by forcing way through very small doorway, opening, or inlet:
squeeze self into (somewhere) through small opening or doorway
push in the head through small opening
force way out through very small outlet, opening or doorway
describes something which is plentiful or falls plentifully:
go out; go for a stroll
take honey from the comb (after driving away the bees)
send representative, ambassador, special messenger, middleman
hurt internally, like pain from septic sore or rheumatic joint
lift down (e.g. pot from the cooking tripod, after the food has been cooked)
tell story; tell story in which song features; tell tale, fable
lift down and out (e.g. pot from the cooking tripod)
choose; choose and take; succeed in choosing the right one; make the right choice:
shout seriously at in order to scare off or to warn
retch; make to feel nausea; cause nausea
sacrifice to ground, regarded as deity
untie; shake off; shake oneself free of
shout and thereby stop someone from doing something:
A. wash breasts, esp. of a newly-delivered mother, to induce breast milk
nine (arch. cf. ìtènaànì): Madụ̀ nọ̀ n'ime ụ̀nụ̀ akwụkwọ dị sannò The people in the school are nine
float; (fig.) be ignorant of what is happening
quarrel (lit. draw words): Mụ̀ nà Èjìọ̀fọ̀ nà-esè okwu Èjìọ̀fọ̀ and myself are quarrelling
pull asunder; tear: Ị nà-àchọ̀ isèka akwụkwọ m? Are you going to tear my book?
carry in hand by handle (e.g. bag, bucket)
lift up; drag up: Ọ chọ̀lị̀ isèkpùni nwata dālu adā She wants to pull up the child who has fallen down
pull together; pull together to the centre
drag into; drag to: Sèkpùnye ín nwa m Give me my child (i.e. Pull my child by the hand and hand her over to me)
draw away forcibly; drag away: Sèkpùpụ̀ nwata afụ̀ nà-atàtọọ̀ ǵụ̀nị̀ ilo Drag that jabbering boy out
steal fowls (habitually, mainly for eating) (lit. draw and eat)
draw out (as bucket from well): Isèpùtà ite n'ime ǵụ̀mị adịrọ̀ ǫlị To pull a pot out from the well is not difficult
draw apart; scatter; spread about; litter; tear by pulling: Jèe sesaa ụmụ aka nà-anụ ǵụ̀ụ Go and separate (or pull apart) the children who are fighting
disgust; be ugly to; be ugly (e.g. faeces or jagged ulcer)
be dried, without juice, as of some fruits and tubers; non-succulent, succulent
grip with teeth: Arụ̄rū̀ tàdò gị na ntị̀ An ant has got its pincers into your ear
instrument for smoothing wet wall, especially of a new building (lit. beater of walls)
stretch hands, fingers; crack the knuckles
club-like wooden instrument shaped like a short pestle and used by native washermen in place of an iron in smoothing thick heavy native clothes (lit. beater of clothes)
construct an akwalị to increase fruitfulness
shout, call for help; raise the alarm
A. praise someone and remind him of what his forefathers did, sometimes to encourage him to undertake new enterprises; chant praise-poetry
bring out spirits in the form of masquerades
chisel, sharpen teeth cosmetically (esp. by Ànam people)
wooden tool for smoothing house walls and floor
bend by beating: Uzu na-etigo mkpisi The blacksmith is beating the spike to
mix; mix with Tigwaa akpụ afụ́ nwan̄tịntị gàlị Add a little garri to that fufu
entrust with: O tìnyèlù ọlù afụ́ n’aka m He entrusted me with the work
pins-and-needles; cramp (= mkpà nsịkọ, ụtanwàngwèlè): Tịtan̄gwèlè nwùlù m I am feeling cramp/pins-and-needles
state of being noised about: Ụ̀zù ya nà-akpọ tìtì Its fame is being noised about
have great swollen belly; develop ascites: Qyà Ọ́fọ̀ èsígo n’ọ̀zịza àghọlu itó afọ Ọ́fọ̀’s illness has passed from general oedema into ascites
be spotted, variegated in colour: Akwụkwọ nìkaa tìlì àgwà ọcha nà èdò This leaf is coloured white and yellow: Nkítá m̄ tìlì àgwà kà agụ́ My dog is spotted like a leopard
move in a weak, flabby way
wake up; make alive; revive; refresh; resuscitate
knock the stick representing the god of justice (ọfọ) on the ground
drum beaten for deities at second burial
native pear; "pear" (Pachylobus edulis Don), baked in hot ashes
ceremonial spear for ọẓọ̄ ceremonies (= alọ̀), and fighting or hunting spears, see asùduù and àgànà
bush-candle tree (Canarium schweinfurthii Engl.). The fruits are cooked by being put in hot water. See also ùbe ọ̀sà.
Canarium schweinfurthii Engl. See also ùbe òkpoko.
A. mind; sense; thought; wisdom; intelligence:
African Star-apple (Chrysophyllum delevoyi De Wild.) and White Star-apple (C. albidum G. Don)
vulture associated with Agwù, an image of which is made
earthenware pot used for storing water; musical pot playing by slapping a hole in the side-wall with the flat of the hand
across the stream, river, etc.; the other side of the river, stream, etc.
A. camwood (dye-wood from the tree *Baphia nitida* Lodd. or *B. pubescens* Hook.f.); red dye from it
mark; track; footprint; trail (e.g. of snake); sunbeam: Nkaa bụ́ ufìlì agwọ̄, ọ bụ́rọ̀ ufìlì igwe This is the trail of a snake, not the track of a bicycle
"eagle", bird valued for its rarity and beauty. Its white feather
watchnight service (e.g. that held on eve of Christmas, New Year, etc.)
general name for fish of the Polypterus and Calamoichthys genera (cf. ọkwo)
Minister in holy orders; pastor; deacon; priest, etc. (lit. messenger of God)
large oblong market basket, made from anà
"walnut" (Tetracarpidium conophorum (Mull Arg.) Hutch. and J.M. Dalz.) (Yoruba aṣàla or awusa)
oil-bean tree or seed (Pentaclethra macrophylla Benth.)
footprint; thing to be followed, e.g. example, precept, statute
broom (considered as a whole bundle of prepared palm fronds)
base of pillar of house; pillar of house
variety of ùlì, whose seeds are very small in size
hole for exit of water from house, compound
sawdust, powder from dry wood as a result of grub activity; inside the wood
rattle, used with ụfị (= ụsākā B.)
West African Black Pepper (*Piper guineense* Schum. and Thonn.); a climber, about 40’ long, whose fruits are used fresh or dried as spices in food and in medicine
path to the back of the compound or outskirts of town
suffer illness; be sick; suffer from disease
be ugly, nauseating: Abụ̀ afụ̀ tị̀asụ̀ n’ànị̀ anyị̀ nà-èyi ḿ oyī The pus which has poured on the floor is ugly to me
put clothes on someone (cf. –yi 1. wear clothes)
put on clothes: Yili àfè gị kà ànyị je Ụ̀kà Put on your clothes and let us go to Church
sift (to separate chaff or foreign body)
pron. you; thou; thee (less common than gị)
bear a name; answer to one’s name
be dedicated to a spirit by taking its name
sweep something over something (e.g. vomit) so as to cover it completely
collapse; slip down; fall down (of wall, house, etc.); sink (of raised path); cave in
dodge; shrink from; beware of; avoid; prevent:
be afraid of; avoid (from fear); be beware of; fear for one’s life
make a palm branch booth on a farm
